{{Short description|State invariant involving qubits}}
In [[quantum information science]], the concurrence is a state invariant involving qubits.

==Definition==
The '''concurrence''' is an [[entanglement monotone]] (a way of measuring entanglement) defined for a mixed state of two [[qubit]]s as:<ref name="Hill1997"/><ref name="Wootters1998"/><ref name="Hildebrand2007"/><ref name="Horodecki2009"/>

:<math> \mathcal{C}(\rho)\equiv\max(0,\lambda_1-\lambda_2-\lambda_3-\lambda_4) </math>

in which <math>\lambda_1,...,\lambda_4</math> are the eigenvalues, in decreasing order, of the Hermitian matrix

:<math>R = \sqrt{\sqrt{\rho}\tilde{\rho}\sqrt{\rho}} </math>

with

:<math>\tilde{\rho} = (\sigma_{y}\otimes\sigma_{y})\rho^{*}(\sigma_{y}\otimes\sigma_{y})</math>
the spin-flipped state of <math>\rho</math> and <math>\sigma_y</math> a [[Pauli spin matrix]]. The complex conjugation <math>{}^*</math> is taken in the eigenbasis of the Pauli matrix <math>\sigma_z.</math> Also, here, for a positive semidefinite matrix <math>A</math>, <math>\sqrt {A}</math> denotes a positive semidefinite matrix <math>B</math> such that <math>B^2=A</math>. Note that <math>B</math> is a unique matrix so defined.

A generalized version of concurrence for multiparticle pure states in arbitrary dimensions<ref>{{Cite journal|author1=P. Rungta|author2=V. Bužek|author3=C. M. Caves|author4=M. Hillery|author5=G. J. Milburn|year=2001|title=Universal state inversion and concurrence in arbitrary dimensions|journal=Phys. Rev. A|volume=64|issue=4 |article-number=042315|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.64.042315|arxiv=quant-ph/0102040|bibcode=2001PhRvA..64d2315R|s2cid=12594864 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bhaskara|first1=Vineeth S.|last2=Panigrahi|first2=Prasanta K.|year=2017|title=Generalized concurrence measure for faithful quantification of multiparticle pure state entanglement using Lagrange's identity and wedge product|journal=Quantum Information Processing|volume=16|issue=5|page=118|doi=10.1007/s11128-017-1568-0|arxiv=1607.00164|bibcode=2017QuIP...16..118B|s2cid=43754114 }}</ref> (including the case of continuous-variables in infinite dimensions<ref name="Swain2022"/>) is defined as:

:<math> \mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{M}}(\rho)=\sqrt{2(1-\text{Tr}\rho^2_{\mathcal{M}})} </math>

in which <math> \rho_{\mathcal{M}} </math> is the reduced [[density matrix]] (or its continuous-variable analogue<ref name="Swain2022"/>) across the bipartition <math> \mathcal{M} </math> of the [[Quantum state|pure state]], and it measures how much the complex amplitudes deviate from the constraints required for tensor separability. The faithful nature of the measure admits necessary and sufficient conditions of separability for pure states.

==Other formulations==
Alternatively, the <math>\lambda_{i}</math>'s represent the square roots of the eigenvalues of the non-Hermitian matrix <math>\rho\tilde{\rho}</math>.<ref name="Wootters1998"/> Note that each <math>\lambda_{i}</math> is a non-negative real number.  From the concurrence, the [[entanglement of formation]] can be calculated.
==Properties==

For pure states, the ''square'' of the concurrence (also known as the ''tangle'') is a polynomial <math>SL(2,\mathbb{C})^{\otimes 2}</math> invariant in the state's coefficients.<ref name="Djocovic2009"/> For mixed states, the concurrence can be defined by [[convex roof extension]].<ref name="Hildebrand2007"/>

For the tangle, there is [[monogamy of entanglement]],<ref name="Coffman2000"/><ref name="Osborne2006"/> that is, the tangle of a qubit with the rest of the system cannot ever exceed the sum of the tangles of qubit pairs which it is part of.
